course_title: Multiliteracies and Numeracy Across Learning Areas
course_description:
Literacy and numeracy are key enabling skills for full and effective participation in and beyond school life. Literate and numerate citizens contribute to the functioning of society and hence literacy and numeracy are a fundamental aspect of education. Literacy and numeracy practices are performed in a multitude of diverse contexts. The term `multiliteracies' acknowledges both the socially diverse (i.e., diverse languages, communication styles and socio-cultural contexts) and multimodal (i.e., any combination of these modes: oral, visual, audio, written, spatial, gestural, tactile) nature of literacy and numeracy practices in the twenty first century. Based on international and Australian research and theory, this course explores multiliteracies meaning making across the curricula, whilst embracing the participatory disposition of today's learners, who interpret, understand, use and create multimodal texts that, for example, incorporate images, video clips, sound effects, music, animation or more specialized representations (mathematical formulas, graphs and tables etc.). Research tells us that it is important to understand how various literacies and various cultural traditions combine these different modalities to make meanings that are more than the sum of what each could mean separately. National and international educational policy recognises both literacy and numeracy as essential foundational skills for success in all learning areas. Teaching strategies to build literacy and numeracy competence as general capabilities for personal enablement, civic and economic participation and social equity are the main focus of this course. The course introduces action research as a framework for professional inquiry, empowering educators to investigate and refine their practice to enhance multiliteracies and numeracy outcomes within their specific learning contexts.

This course may not be offered In Person if the enrolment is less than 10 students.

This course explores literacy and numeracy as interdisciplinary skills for meaning making and analysis across all sectors of society. The complexity of social, cultural and political issues pertaining to literacy and numeracy are critically examined and possible pathways forward are mapped that employ up-to-date research and theory on effective pedagogical strategies for literacy and numeracy education.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate comprehensive and well-founded knowledge of the current nature of literacy and numeracy in the twenty first century
Critically review contemporary international and national empirical research on literacy and numeracy learning across curricula
Apply contemporary international and national empirical research on literacy and numeracy learning to teaching and learning design across learning areas
Design an action research project that investigates an aspect of multiliteracies and/or numeracy teaching and learning as a means of professional development and pedagogical improvement.

assessment_details.title: Action Research Problem statement, Literature Review and Inquiry Questions
assessment_details.task_description: Reflecting on the benefits of action research for professional learning is a useful way of improving your understanding of your role as a practitioner and as an educational researcher. Across EDUC7113 the contemporary landscape of multiliteracies and numeracy will be mapped and explored. With this understanding you will identify a key multiliteracy or numeracy challenge or issue that you will explore across the semester. This will be the focus of Assessment 1, 2 and 3. Assessment Task 1 is the beginning of your action research project proposal. It consists of identifying the inquiry/problem, conducting a literature review and creating research questions. Assessment Task 1 has 3 parts, and will be up to 2000 words total (excluding references): Part 1 – Problem Statement (approx. 250 words) Action research in education is a cyclical, reflective research practice that many experienced teachers engage in. It often involves choosing a topic, framing the research problem statement and formulating specific research question/s (guided by the literature review) (Efron & David, 2020). In Part 1 you are to define your inquiry focus by briefly describing the educational context and the challenge or issue you wish to address as a problem statement . You will be required to share your research topic, problem statement and potential research question/s (on the Blackboard Discussion and during class in week 2 or 3) to receive feedback from the Lecturer and your peers. Part 2 – Literature Review (approx.1500 words) Conduct a literature review of the challenge or issue you identified in Part 1. Gather information from peer-reviewed academic literature, policies, reports, etc. to situate your problem within education context/s Consolidate all this information into a literature review demonstrating synthesis, critical analysis, evaluation and identification of any gaps in research. Discuss how this literature shapes your understanding of the topic and how it helps you justify your inquiry . Part 3 – Research Question(s) (approx. 250 words) Identify your key research question/s you are going to investigate Explain how it/they are informed by your literature review References Efron, E.E, & Ravid, R. (2020). Action Research in Education : A Practical Guide , Guilford Publications https://ebookcentral.proquest.com/lib/uql/detail.action?docID=5928892 Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Action Research Project Proposal
assessment_details.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Presentation, Portfolio, Poster
assessment_details.task_description: For this task you will communicate your plan for your action research project in a format you feel best communicates the proposal. This choice is open to oral, written, presentation. audio-visual product, or a combination of the above. You may submit up to 2000 words, a presentation of up to 12 mins, poster, or a multimodal product of an equivalent length. Your submission in any of the formats, should cover: Introduction: Briefly describe the research context and your problem statement (from Task 1) and describe how your literature review informed your research questions Methodology: Describe the actions you will undertake and justify them with the research literature Data, Analysis and Discussion: Describe the data you propose to collect and how you will analyse it (including teaching strategy or lesson plan, etc. you intend to implement for the research). Explain how your findings will answer your research questions and how this may inform your future practice. Create an implementation plan with timeline Conclusion and implications: Reflect on what you have learned through your action research proposal, what implications your project might raise and how it may influence your future practice Read full task description Hide full task description
